title: On the maximum size of $(a,b)$-town (mod $k$) families
summary: For integers $n \geq k \geq 2$ and $0 \leq a,b \leq k-1$, let $m_{k,n}(a,b)$ denote the maximum size of an $(a,b)$-town (mod $k$) family of an $n$-element set, a collection of subsets of whose cardinalities are congruent to $a$ modulo $k$ and whose pairwise intersections are congruent to $b$ modulo $k$. This notion generalizes the classical Oddtown and Eventown problems. We prove that $m_{k,n}(a,b)\leq n$ whenever $a\not\equiv b\pmod{k}$, thereby resolving a conjecture of Veselinov and Marinov.
